utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-96-21-T.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, I have one matter before cross-examination. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Remind the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr Babic, may I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, we just have one matter to bring to the court's attention before we begin cross-examination; that is that the defence received a letter from the prosecution on February 28th listing a whole list of documents provided by the Bosnian government finally, and after we received the letter, the defence requested to review the documents. They were reviewed and then a request was made for a copy of certain documents. Those documents were just provided to the defence on Thursday, March 13th, and we have been unable to get two of the documents translated into English. They are very important to the cross-examination of this witness. The Registrar's office is working diligently with us right now to solve this matter. They have assured us it will be solved by noon. I wanted to ask the court's tolerance. We do need that document just in case we have completed with cross-examination to allow us to get that document before the total completion of this cross-examination. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Where are we at the cross-examination stage? Can we continue from that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to your instructions the defence would like to inform you that the beginning of the cross-examination will be done by defence counsel Tapuskovic defending Pavo Mucic. After that the cross-examination will be taken over by Ms McMurrey on behalf of Esad Landzo, and after that Mr Moran on behalf of the defence of Hazim Delic, and the fourth to cross-examine will be lawyer Edina Residovic defending Zejnil Delalic. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much for underlining the order in which the cross-examination is to took place. Can you now proceed the way you have defined it? Cross-examination by MR TAPUSKOVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I shall begin, as agreed by the defence, so that I shall be the first to address a number of questions to the witness Babic. Mr Babic, I am defence counsel of Pavo Mucic and I would like to ask you to answer a few questions. The first thing I would like to ask you is as follows. When Pavo Mucic on 1st September 1992 at the end of the conversation with you, he addressed you with the polite "you". Did he use this "you", the polite form of "you" throughout that conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I saw Mr Pavo in building number 6 on the 1st September, when he came and called me out. I went out and that is all I know. I know he came once again. I am just --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask that later. I am asking you about that particular conversation. How long did it last between the two of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very brief. He just said "get up" and I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that your only direct contact in Celebici with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did you do after this conversation with him? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did nothing but I went out and the International Red Cross was about 15 metres from the door. They had some lists and they were taking notes. There was a van waiting for us and then they took us to the Musala Sports Hall in Konjic. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine but what I am interested in is the van that you climbed into. Can you describe it for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how to describe it. I know we call it a combi, a combi-van. It is closed. It has a casing. The door is somewhere in the middle. The driver sits down and that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much space was there inside? When you climbed in, were there other people inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Quite a number. I cannot remember. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the moment that you climbed in, how many people were inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. There were a lot of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those people who climbed in -- did they talk to Mucic before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can tell you that Mr Mucic and Hazim Delic, they went along and asked about weapons,. Every fourth and every fifth they would call out and take outside and that is how my turn came. I went out and got into the combi. There were lots of other people inside and that is how I got to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cannot even tell us roughly how many people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all prisoners from the same hangar as you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of any single one of those persons inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Scepo Vukalo. He is my neighbour. I remember him. Bozo Tomic, also a neighbour of mine from Bijelovcina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Davor Bendo, also my neighbour from the village of Bijelovcina I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was driving the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. A driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a driver -- was he from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know; I do not know. I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is when you left Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that was the only van taking people from Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that it took me to Musala. I do not know about others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Musala, did you see any people there who were previously in Celebici and now they were in Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember. There were some people who left number 6 in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but were they in Musala when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this conversation that you had with Mucic, the only one you had, you said that you saw him once again; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I didn't know him at the time but other people told me who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not talk to him then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just saw him talking to a man called Tarzan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was at the entrance to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear what they were talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they talking in whispers or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he address anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he just spoke to him. Maybe he knew him. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, you mentioned a motor. How did he get to the entrance of the hangar. You said he made two steps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. About 9 o'clock in the morning I heard the sound of a motor engine and people said that Pavo was coming and then he would come in front of the hangar, but the door was closed. Then maybe five or ten minutes later we heard -- we would hear the sound of the engine again and he would disappear. No, I didn't see him when he came. He would not enter. I saw him only once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interested that he was wearing a camouflage uniform. Was he wearing that uniform both times when he spoke to you and this other time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Both times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he was on a motorcycle did he wear -- was he wearing anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see him. He did not enter number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who this man is, this man Tarzan? Did you learn later on what his name is, his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I think he was from Gradina, the village of Gradina, from the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him ever again afterwards? Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that day that the Red Cross came three times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned on 12th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said somewhere around the 1st or 2nd they came and then ten days later about the 12th, and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the day that you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. That was the third time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were there three times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the first time you said the visit lasted two hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you determine how long the previous visits lasted the second time on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, maybe also about one to two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They asked you individually to show your injuries. Was that all they did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they entered us in a registrar. They asked when we were brought there and so on. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. May we ask defence counsel and witness to slow down a little there? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. When they came for the second time you said they were there again for two hours. Was the purpose of their visit the same as the previous time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that all they did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I just know they took down our names, they registered us, and they asked us to show our injuries, and then they took note of that and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Red Cross left, you said on Wednesday that conditions improved, that you were allowed visitors and that you received food. Who enabled this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the Red Cross came and left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who allowed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I just know that it was easier for us and we were told that it was the International Red Cross, together with the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the commanders of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the Red Cross was no longer there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who allowed visitors to see you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not see any representatives. They did not come. We just received bags of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who allowed this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one more thing to ask you. When you went in the direction of the camp did the soldiers search you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally? Did you have anything personally on you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you entered the camp you had nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who is Ismeta Pozder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she in the camp on the day you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said that on 23rd September, yes, when I -- no, no, in May, not September, when I and Slobodan Babic went from the Musala Sports Hall by truck; we reached Radava. It is a hotel. It is 1 km from Radava to Musala. When we entered that hotel that is when we saw Ismeta Pozder. What she was doing, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see her in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Any other cross-examination? Cross-examined by MISS McMURREY

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If I might use the podium because I have all these papers; would you mind? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Feel free.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. May it please the court. May I proceed? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr Babic. My name is Cynthia McMurrey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have never met before you came into the court room, have we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On February 20th, 1996 you visited with the prosecutor, did you not? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Is the witness hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sorry. On February 26th, 1996, you visited with the prosecutor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where did I meet with the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You offered a sworn statement on February 26th, 1996 for the prosecution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did make such a statement. I made a statement in February, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also in the last month the prosecution notified you that I would like an opportunity to visit you too, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, they told you that we would like to come to Bijelovcina and visit with you, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the prosecution never notified you that the defence wanted to visit with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we did not get an opportunity to visit with you before your testifying in court, did we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, did you refresh your memory with any document before testifying on Wednesday or today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't use any documents. I just said what I saw and what I lived through and that is what is imprinted in my mind, what I felt on my own skin and that is what I could talk about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you have testified, you had a long meeting with the prosecution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They prepared you for testifying. Who were the other people that were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do -- I do not know. I do not know any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other witnesses from Bosnia at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. No, I was alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question: the interpreter for your statement, the person you spoke to when you made your statement on February 20th: she was Serbian, was she not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you described in your testimony on Wednesday that you were a forester, did you not, by profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am a forester.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are -- I want to remind you, Mr Babic, that you are under oath. I know the court did that already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you were a forester, it has been alleged by people in your community that you took money to allow people to cut trees illegally at that point. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is an absolute lie. It is an insult for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the truth is that Mr Turone asked you on Wednesday that you were a forester by profession whenever the war broke out, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Four or five months ago I retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you have not been a forester for quite a while, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, about five months before the war, I retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you retired, you were terminated from that job, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not know. Whoever had 28 years of service and was of a certain age, he was laid off, and that is what happened to me. So I retired. I got some kind of an administrative pension, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were working as a forester, you were also employed at Pilana; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The Timber Industrial Enterprise, Konjic. It is a timber industry enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you worked at Pilana along with Mr Landzo's father, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was about 1966, 1967. Yes, we worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth of the matter is that you were fired from the job at Pilana because you were caught drinking on the job, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is your testimony before this court today that you were not terminated from your job at Pilana because of drinking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This is not relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, any time this witness has testified, his credibility is at issue. Therefore, I have a right to go into whether he is telling the truth about the thing he testified on on direct examination. He testified he was a forester whenever the war broke out. That is not true. He also testified just then that he was not fired from his job and we will be able to present evidence that he was at a later date. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact, Mr Babic, the people in your community might say that you have a drinking problem, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is just propaganda, lies and insults against me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is no truth then to someone in your community saying that you had an accident on the job at Pilana, whereby you were drunk and you fell into some hot plaster. That is not true; is that what you are telling this tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. There is no truth in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You say that you come from the village -- and pardon my pronunciation of these -- Bijelovcina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you go by a nickname, Jaranica; do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Jaranica" means "little friend"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a Bosnian Serb, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in Bosnia, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore you are a citizen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Village of Bijelovcina, Konjic, Herzegovina, but all this used to be part of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are a citizen of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in times gone by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are right now, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean you have forfeited your citizenship of the country today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The most important thing is in April and May of 1992 and June and July and August of 1992 you were a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you voted or you could have voted in the March 1st, referendum, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you vote in that referendum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are an active member of the SDS, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was. I was not active, but I was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were an active member of the SDS in 1992, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you signed a sworn statement for the prosecution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Hold on for a moment. What is SDS?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Would you tell the judges of this tribunal what SDS stand for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What does it mean, not what does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: SDP?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I think it is called SDS. For us it would be SDP but for them it is another word meaning the same thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is known as SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to make it clear so the court understands that the leader of the SDS in Bosnia-Herzegovina that represented us in the assembly was a man named Radovan Karadzic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I do not know exactly who represented me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean you do not know who Radovan Karadzic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not interested in that. I wish nobody had represented me. It would have been better if I had stayed to live in Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina in a nice country among our people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is a shame. That is true, but the way it was in 1992 was there was a definite split in the parties. There was the SDS and then there was the Bosnian Muslim party also, was there not, the SDA? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: What is his answer to that? Let us hear his answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 you were considered the leader of the SDS party in your village, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is your testimony before this tribunal today that you were not considered a leader of the Serbian party in your community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not consider me that. I was not interested in that. I was 60 years old. I was not interested in anything any more. I got a pension and all I wanted was to live quietly a few more days, to enjoy our freedom that we used to have, to be able to walk around and take it easy. I never thought until then that war would ever break out. Nobody could have persuaded me that a war would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The witness is not answering the question. He is going into a narrative. Could you please limit his question to -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He was explaining to you that he was never interested in those things thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, in your statement on February 20th, 1996 you demonstrated to this court that you were aware of what was happening in Bosnia Herzegovina at the time, were you not? In fact, you began your statement with: "When the Croat and Muslim part of the Sarajevo Assembly seceded, we got scared", did you not? So you were aware of what was happening, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can answer that question. May I answer that question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 4th April 1992 we heard that Bosnia-Herzegovina had seceded from Yugoslavia and somehow this was a problem, because we were already scared. So we had to look after our homes and stables because we were afraid someone might attack us, because I had experience from the previous world wars, and if I may tell you about that experience and how it was that we were scared that we might get killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would just like to ask. You said you heard that the Croat Muslim part of the Sarajevo Assembly seceded. You heard that on your radio, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I know people were talking about it. I cannot remember I heard it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You possessed a radio in your home, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't have a radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your neighbours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived alone as a bachelor in one room. So I didn't have much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did listen to the radio, did you not, in your community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't really listen to it, to tell you the truth. I do not listen to it even today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the truth of the matter is that the Croat and Muslim part of the Sarajevo Assembly did not secede at all, did they? The Serbian part of the coalition walked out of the Assembly in 1991, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not meddle in those things. I do not know anything about politics and those things. Who seceded, what seceded. All I know is what I heard, what I just said and I do not know anything else and I was not interested in anything else. I cannot answer those questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your fear stemmed from the fact that there was a break between the Croats and Muslims and the Serbians in the assembly in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This is not part of the direct examination of the witness and he already said he does not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond, he signed a sworn statement that was provided to all of us, and he begins his statement with telling us about the political atmosphere. I believe that the defence has a right to go into his knowledge about such statements. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can cross-examine but you will take the consequences of whatever comes from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware. Thank you. Now, the talk in your community: you were aware of who Radovan Karadzic was and you were aware that he gave a speech talking about the disappearance of the Muslim people, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware that the Serbians began the aggression in this war, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This is not part of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not interfere in politics. I do not know anything about those things. Do not ask me such questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if there are other witnesses that will come forward before this tribunal and testify that you helped organise the Serbian resistance in your village, they are going to be lying, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour, for the same reasons already stated by me. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are false witnesses in my view. They are not telling the truth if they say such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Many Serbs in your village were armed, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I was not. I had what I had. As I said, I had a pistol with a licence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when MUP, the military police, came to your village and asked you to turn over your weapons peacefully, you did not, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said at the end when they finished with me, then they asked me where my pistol was and I went with them and showed them where it was. On the spot I bent down. I gave the pistol. He took the pistol, tore up the licence and that was all. I said that in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr Babic. You also said when you were asked to turn over your weapon, you went and hid it under a rock, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was when I started fleeing, when the Muslims attacked my village with Boro Ivkovic I did hide it under a rock. I didn't want to carry it on me, and that was how I gave my pistol to Mitke Pirkic afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know the military police came first and asked everybody to turn over their weapons peacefully, did they not, and you refused to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No-one asked me to hand over weapons. If they had asked me to, I would have given them in. I didn't need that pistol anyway any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Dusan Bendzo was the Serb responsible for distributing arms in your village, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He made his own statement. What he did he knows. He made his own statement. He knows what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you state that people in your village were not armed, if witness Risto Vukolo comes and testifies and says: "There were more than 20 people armed in Bijelovcina", then he would be lying, would he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He will make his own statement. He will tell you what happened. Everyone is responsible for himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the SDS in your community, you met with the other people -- the other members of the community, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We neighbours would meet. Of course we would meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also promised by the JNA that if you held out, they would come and save you, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the JNA help did not materialise, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that you have an immediate loss of memory in this area when you do meet with other members of the community, the members of the SDS and you do not remember what you talked about; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember what I talked about with my neighbours. We talked about what we were going to do, what we were going to plant, about our fields and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You stated that you were scared in your statement: "Scared, although we did not know what to be scared of". Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the truth is you knew what had begun in 1991 and you knew who began it, did you not? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not think he could answer that. He has already denied it, that he did not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know what was going to happen. I didn't know. Only we knew that something was wrong. I remember the Second World War in 1941, when Hitler occupied Yugoslavia. I know my mother took me to hide in a cave, and we somehow survived, and that is what we expected in this war would happen, the war that broke out in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. I also thought that the best thing was to flee to the woods and the caves and afterwards we would all come back home. That is the experience I had of seeking shelter in the woods and the caves, but this war was not like that. This war forced all three peoples to flee, to seek shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to the caves, if Mr Vukalo says you hid your weapons in a cave, is he going to be lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not in a cave. It was under a stone. It was a big rock of two or three kilos and it was not a cave, next to a little wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to go back to your testimony on Wednesday. You said that when you were arrested, the only thing that you could remember was that you saw the TO, the territorial defence insignia on the soldiers that arrested you and that you could not notice anything else; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not what you said on February 20th, 1996, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, your statement, your sworn statement from February 20th, 1996, you talked more about the Croats being the soldiers who mistreated you, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you said they were wearing HOS insignias and Ustasha insignias. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could not remember that on Wednesday, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did say that I saw one. I recognised him, Mlikota Zeljko. He was a Croat and I recognised him and he had that on his left arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to refresh your memory from page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- from 255 of the record from Wednesday. Mr Turone asked you: "Question: Do you remember if any of them had some insignia? Answer: I saw there was a 'TO' on the arm. That was what was written there. I could not notice anything else"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were lying on Wednesday, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not lying. I said that on Wednesday. Yes, I saw on the left arm "TO", and nothing else was there. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but on February 20th 1996 your main statement was that they were all Croatian. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not remember that, that it was the majority, but there were five, six, maybe ten Croats who wore that. They wore that and they were with the Muslims when we went with Mitko and Sejo. They went to the right, separated out, and Mithat and ourselves went towards the left towards Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth is the TO forces were not just Croat forces in 1992. They were Croat and Muslim forces, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that is how I explained it. I didn't know how else to explain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but there was no such thing in 1992 as strictly a Muslim force, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the HVO, the Croatian soldiers, participated in your arrest and transported you to Celebici, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They just arrested me together with the Muslim soldiers and then they escorted us halfway through and then they left. Then I stayed with the Mithat soldiers, and the Mithat soldiers took me to Musala and then I never saw the HVO group again, where they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, excuse me. Could I ask the court just to instruct Mr Babic to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There has been five years. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Remember I told you when you are cross-examining, you take the consequences of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I do not believe he is answering my question. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He is answering what he understood you asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr Babic, you claimed when you were arrested that the Croatian and Muslim forces beat you severely. Is that what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated you lost your teeth, you were covered with blood, etc, etc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they took you into a separate room, did they not? In your statement you said there were two Muslim women and about 15 HOS soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you know a man named -- pardon my pronunciation; I may have to spell it -- Zeljko Mlikota? It is M-L-I-K-O-T-A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is how I remember. I knew him so I recognised him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew he was a Croatian, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I knew that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Croatian man is the one who made you drink three glasses of his urine, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and two others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Then he also watched while two women undid your pants, took out pincers and tongs and with a razor blade were about to cut your penis off, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was the Muslim Mithat Pirkic that made them stop, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who was the starter. Maybe it was Midhat. I was lost at that time. I did not know. I do not know how long it went on. I do not know the exact number. I had given you at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr Babic, in your statement from February 20th, 1996 you stated that at that point Mithat Pirkic told them to stop, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever I was beaten, he would say "stop". He said "stop".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the end he said: "It has been enough of abuse."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know another Croat named Ivica Buric, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't know this Ivica Buric, not at all. I do not remember that. There has been five years and I have forgotten quite a bit. I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot remember another Croatian soldier named Josic Aga?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was not there. I know him. He is a neighbour from my village. That one I know. He is a Croat and he was not there at all. Aga Josic, no, he was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was not there at the arrest but you did see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw him at Celebici during your stay there, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did say military police and HVO soldiers were at the Celebici while you were there, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at Celebici, you did see other soldiers other than the TO? You saw HVO soldiers and the military police present at Celebici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, I have been sick. I was not interested in anything. What I could see, there were camouflage uniforms and that is all I remember. How many, who they were ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you finally arrived at Musala in Konjic you and Slobodan Babic were interviewed by three investigators, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken out and in your statement on Wednesday you said that these investigators asked you a lot of stupid questions. Did you not say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not stupid. Some questions, not stupid questions. That is not what I said. Maybe I was not properly understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I believe the record says that you called them "stupid questions". I just wanted to ask you: the stupid questions were things like "were you a member of the SDS and did you have a weapon?", were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. Do not. Please, lady, do not misrepresent that. Those were not stupid questions. Those were the questions whether I was a SDS member, and I said "yes". They were not stupid people. That is not what I said. I do not know who said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, this was an investigative group made up of Croats, Muslims and people from the military police, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who it was composed of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this investigation by a joint committee was the proper procedure under the circumstances, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand you exactly. Could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the circumstances when there has been war and armed conflict and detainees are brought in, the proper procedure would be that an investigative group would come in and interview the detainees to see what category they would fit in. That is a proper procedure under these circumstances, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was called out once and then I came out and I do not know who it was. They asked me what weapons I had. I answered and that took about five minutes, not more. Then I went back. Then others were brought out, and I was never brought out again, so I do not know what else to say about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go back and refer to page 267 of the transcript from Wednesday, line 225: "I was ordered to sit in the corner. Then they asked me some stupid questions like did I vote for the SDS." That is what you said on Wednesday, was it not? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually, he had answered that "that is not how I said that".

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: For impeachment purposes he said he did not say it and the record is clear that he did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. Please. Wherever I was asked whether I was a member of SDS, I always said I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. After you were interviewed at Musala, you were then taken to a place called Radava, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but that was the next day, on 23rd in the evening, 23rd May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and Slobodan Babic were both taken to this Radava, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were held there for two days, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is not true. We were there about half an hour in this hotel, about half an hour. That is what I said on Wednesday and also on 26th I said -- of 1992 I said the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were at Radava you also --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because if you had not understood me, two days later I saw Slobodan Babic in number 22. That is wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said you were taken to Radava on 23rd; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you also stated that you reached Celebici on 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent the night -- the 23rd, yes. Let me tell you. On 22nd in the evening we were brought to Musala in the sports centre. We spent the night there. On 23rd we came to Radava, to the hotel, and then -- that is what I talked about on Wednesday. From Radava on 23rd in the evening I went to the number 22 in Celebici. So please do not take me back and forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, what you did testify to is while you were at Radava is when you and Slobodan Babic were beaten the most severely; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as we walked in there were three or four of them. One had a foot bandaged. I do not know what had happened to his foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you were beaten the most severely at Radava, what you also testified to was that Slobodan Babic received his mortal wounds at Radava, not at Celebici. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I stated that Slobodan Babic, I did not see him when we left the hotel Radava. I got on to the truck and I do not recall -- I do not recall anything about Slobodan Babic. I know that two days later I saw him in the number 22 in Celebici and he was very bad, and I heard that he had been beaten and then for two days that he had died or something, but they all brought him. He had not died, and they brought him to number 22. That is what I heard, and then he was there five, six or eight days, and then they took from Celebici and I never heard from him again. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify for the tribunal that in your statement of February 20th, 1996 you said that when Mr Slobodan Babic had been brought to Celebici he had already been tortured. He had lost his sight. Apparently lost his hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His arm was all mutilated. His throat was all mutilated and your last statement in the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this happened in Radava? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually he appears to be confirming that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about Radava. I do not know where it happened, whether it was in Radava, but I never saw him, but do not say what I have not said. I didn't say his eyes were massacred or something. He could not see. I also said about his mouth, that it was severely wounded. That is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that you are claiming that this did not happen at Radava?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know where it happened, whether it was in Radava or where. That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I approach --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I approach the witness? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If you are cross-examining, I have told you that you are cross-examining and you take the consequences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I just want him to see in his prior sworn statement -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Put that to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: In your prior sworn statement, the last sentence on the second paragraph -- I mean, the first paragraph of the second page you stated: "This happened in Radava". Were you lying then or are you lying now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I object to calling the witness a liar, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Were you telling the truth then or are you telling the truth now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard that this is what happened at Radava, that he got these wounds at Radava. After I left the prison, I was sitting with Dr Petko Grubac, and he told me this happened to Slobodan somewhere in the school in Konjic. Petko Grubac knows that precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My only last question concerning Slobodan Babic is his injuries which caused his death happened before he reached Celebici, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He came just like me, all in blood, covered in blood and beaten up from Radava, same as I was, and after that I really do not know what happened to him, how it all happened that he came there all beaten up and what happened. I really do not know nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You were held in building number 22 when you first arrived at Celebici, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is a small building behind the main building when you come into the gate, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, that was -- that was a compound that was built by the Yugoslav army. I had never been there before. It was night and I was put in number 22. I know that it was rectangular. One side was longer than the other. I do not know how many there were in there. I do not recall much. I remember Slobodan. I remember seeing him two days later. I do not know whether he had been at Radava, but two days later I saw him. He was in a very bad shape. He was wounded, and I don't recall anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, when you were held in building number 22, it was not an infirmary at that time, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was merely a place for the detainees to be held until their status was determined by the investigators, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you were held there in number 22 until you had your second meeting with the investigative group; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you went through the same procedure again, where an investigative body came and asked you questions to determine what your status was at the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know what my status was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were trying to determine that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not told anything. I do not know anything about that. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The entire chamber will rise now and reassemble at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can continue that cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I have one question to ask before the break. We have a doctor here who would like to look at Mr Babic's -- I am sorry. I would like to ask permission to have our doctor look at the witness during the break. (Short break) (11.30am) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Get the witness in so we will continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just take up a little housekeeping matter before we proceed, I have a Dutch doctor, Dr de Kroot outside. I have asked him to come to examine the ankle of Mr Babic. The prosecution is opposed to the examination so I am asking the court if there is some way that they can resolve this. Dr de Kroot has surgery set in 30 minutes at the hospital, so he either has to do it immediately or he is available after 6 o'clock today, if the witness could be made available for examination at that time. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually I do not know the background for this examination, because if it is coming through the cross-examination, the relevant background for questioning injury should have been laid, and I have not heard of any question questioning the background of whatever injury that has been complained of.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will be getting to the questioning about his injury, but on direct examination he testified about his injury and showed the defence counsel, and there are no medical records, and there is no other documentation about the injury. So eventually it is going to become mandatory to have some kind of medical examination of Mr Babic. I was just trying to save judicial economy and to save poor Dr de Kroot -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I would not say it is poor cross-examination, but if there is no evidence of injury, no medical evidence of anything that has happened to him, what is your business?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are no medical records, but he showed his leg in the court room. I would just like a doctor to determine whether that is a burn scar or a bruise, or the possible age of his injury. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please let us get the witness in: (Witness returned to court) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please remind him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr Babic, I would like to remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May it please the court. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can start.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Babic, I believe when we left off that I was questioning you about building number 22. In building number 22 in your statement of February 20th 1996 you are claimed that you said to the prosecution that you and 100 other Serbs were held in that room for 20 something days without urinating, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that room is about 2 metres by 2 metres, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. When I made my statement, the judge asked me: "Do you know how big that room is, how long, how wide it is? Tell me how many people there were. Tell me." I said: "I do not know. How do I know? I didn't count them, but there were lots of us. There was no room to sit down. I do not know how many people were there." That is what I said and I still do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe my question for you was the room was 2 metres by 2 metres, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know I am telling you. Later on -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: She wants to get the size of the room. That is why she's asking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: In your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please allow me to say I thought it was maybe 5 by 4, but I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement on February 20th 1996 you told the interpreter and the prosecution that the room was about 2 metres by 2 metres, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I maybe said that, but I said: "I do not know. I do not know." Then he insisted and I said: "I do not know; I do not know. I cannot remember."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now on Wednesday of last week you had a severe loss of memory from the time that you made your statement on February 26th, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Excuse me. What was the objection, so that I may respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is a question aiming at confusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is cross-examination, and he said on Wednesday that: "I can no longer remember anything about the infirmary." His claim was: "I cannot remember anything. I was lost. I remember I was there. I simply do not know." That is contrary to what he said on February 20th, 1996. That is the purpose of the question. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: What is your question now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The question is that he had a severe loss of memory between February 20th, 1996 and last Wednesday. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: That is a very technical question and can only be addressed to a specialist, not this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Your witness on Wednesday was quite different from your statement that you made on February 20th, 1996, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Five years has gone by. I have forgotten a lot of it. I know what I saw and that is what I said, and I cannot answer any other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, on 20th you said there were 100 Serbs in the building and on Wednesday you said merely that it was densely populated, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said on 26th February too that I didn't know how many people there were. The judge told me: "Give us an approximation", and I said: "I do not know. It looked to me as if there were 500. How do I know how many there were. I had lost consciousness then and my memory and everything." I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 20th February 1996 you never mentioned that you lost consciousness or that you were having a memory problem or that you were sick, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, what you are saying here is that the statement that you made on February 19th 1996 is not accurate; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I won't say that. I will never say that; it is not correct. I just said that I couldn't remember. I do not know enough about 22, how many prisoners there were inside. How do I know? I was lost. I was sick at the time, and I can't say any more than I have said. Also on 26th February 1996, when I answered questions I remember that I was put in that room as soon as I got there, and I do not remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On February --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In another five years I'll probably forget everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On February 20th 1996 you never told the judge or you never reflected in your signed statement that you couldn't remember anything, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't say. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, that has only come up since your testifying in this court room, has it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have said that on 26th February, when I was making my statement. I saw that the judge wanted to make it a bit shorter, to hurry me up a little, and that is how it came about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you were very specific in your statement on February 20th, 1996, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was specific, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not have a watch or anything and you said you were in that room for exactly 22 days and you had never gone to the toilet. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said in your statement that you saw a pump in building number 22. Immediately after that you said you did not know what kind of machine it was. Did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I was able to tell, it was some kind of a pump or a machine. I do not know. What I said was what I thought it was when I saw it. Whether it was a pump or a machine, I saw some fire hoses. That is as far as I can remember, nothing more. Whether it was a pump or a machine, I really do not know. Do not ask me that. I cannot give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you were specifically held in building 22 for 22 days and that you never even went outside for the toilet?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. The statement done in February 1996 speaks for itself. So defence counsel may introduce it, if she wants, but asking the witness to characterise that statement is improper, according to the opinion of the prosecution, improper and unfair to the witness. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I respond? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is a prior sworn statement by the witness and as a prior sworn statement the defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. This is not a sworn statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it the statement or not of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: It is a statement done in front of the prosecuting investigator by the witness but not under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If there are any contradictions between the two statements, how can she use the contradictions unless she can address the witness with those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have no objection to introducing this statement into the court. This would be probably a clear way of acting, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: May I advise counsel for the defence? If you intend to contradict this witness with a statement made outside these proceedings, you should tell that. That is the only way you can bring both of them into conflict, but using them outside the proceedings will not disclose this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness signed each and every page of this statement. Also it is witnessed and acknowledged that he received it in his language. The statement was voluntarily given. It was read back to him in his name and he -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: But it is not evidence in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not offering it -- I am offering it for impeachment purposes only. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Then it has to be part of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I am only aware of the rules of evidence in my country, and I am asking the court -- I think in Great Britain and in the United States and under most Common Law countries a prior sworn statement can be used for impeachment purposes. I do not have the obligation to admit it into evidence. If the prosecution chooses to, then they should. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You have to, because you cannot take evidence outside the proceedings to contradict the proceedings itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But you will have to produce the statement after the cross-examination is over as part of the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be happy to do that after this is over. If the court would like to follow along, I would be happy. I have no other copy except my marked on copy, but if you would like. I would like the court to be also aware of his contradictions in his two statements. If I had another copy, I would provide it for you right now. If I get my hands on a clean copy, I will certainly tender it to the court for the record. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Proceed as you like. My experience is firstly the background about the discrepancy between what he has said here and what you have in his extra-judicial statement and then you put that extra-judicial statement in as the evidence. Then you can cross-examine on it. It appears you are doing it in the wrong way round, because now you are telling us things which happened outside the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will be happy to comply with the request of this court. It is unfamiliar to me, but I have no objections to the court's request, and if you will just allow me to cross-examine from the statement, I will offer it -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I did not interrupt you. You were cross-examining him on what he said outside here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will be happy to comply with the court's request. I do not think you want my marked-up copy. I will try to provide a clean copy for you. Okay. May I proceed? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can carry on as best as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I try to do that all the time. Thank you. Mr Babic, you said that you were held in building number 22 for 22 days without going outside, and are you telling this tribunal that you did not count how many people were in the building with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll tell you that I said that I do not know how many people were in that room. I know that there was little water, little food. I couldn't eat. So about 22 days I didn't go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: you mean you did not count the people in a 2 by 2 metre room with you for 22 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Mr Turone also asked you if you could recognise the building, the Celebici, and you told Mr Turone that you could not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. You told Mr Turone that you could not recognise them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the fact is you have seen the Celebici barracks before, have you not, because you can see them from your village, can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see them, yes. I saw them. I know there was a railway line, and below the railway line there was a road, but I never went there, nor do I know what it looked like. I came there by night and I didn't look around. I just looked in front of me. I was not interested in anything any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That Celebici barracks has been there for many years, has it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the building was built by the Yugoslav Army. I do not know when, how many years before the war. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am kind of clumsy at using these tools that this court has, but I have a drawing on the ELMO and I do not know how to turn it on. Could I ask somebody to assist me with that for the next question? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Whose drawing is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to ask him to identify if it is an accurate drawing of something -- of the inside of hangar 6, if he can identify it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You want to ask this witness to tell you if your own drawing is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I believe it is accurate, but I would like for him to authenticate it. Could I ask the witness to stand and approach the drawing? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Babic, would you look at the drawing that is right in front of you? I would like you to approach the original that is over there, because I want you to put a mark on it, if possible. Does this drawing accurately reflect the inside of hangar number 6 when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can remember a little bit but I cannot tell from this drawing. I do not know whether it is a drawing of the hangar. I know there was an entrance and there were four rows of prisoners, two round the edges and two in the middle. If that is that building, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The red lines, do they reflect where the prisoners were sitting in hangar number 6, around the edges with two lines in the middle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see the prisoners, but according to these lines, yes, we did sit one next to another and then the second row and a third row. We did sit one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your February 20th, 1996 statement you stated that you sat the sixth place in the second row, and on Wednesday you said you were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The third row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On Wednesday you said you were seated the sixth place in the third row. Which one was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the third row, here somewhere. I was sixth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, could you take that pink marker and just mark on that drawing to your right where you were seated for months in hangar 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell looking at this map, but here somewhere (indicating). I was in the third row, sixth from the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just asking you to estimate but if you could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you on this map. I cannot say. This is all very rough, because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not have -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Do you not think that is conclusive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here somewhere (indicating). JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He says he cannot say. Is that not sufficient for his opinion?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to ask him to estimate in row three where he sat. He was there for several months and he had an assigned seat. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: That was your question and he says he cannot say. That was what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Is that true, Mr Babic? You cannot estimate where you were sitting in row three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking exactly. Can you just estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gentlemen, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, go ahead and sit down then and we will skip the interior of the hangar number 6. You do know that Milovan Kuljanin, or Mitke, sat close to you, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know some of my neighbours who were sitting next to me, close to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know whether Zeljko Klimenta sat next to you either or close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Klimenta was sitting across from me. Branko Gotovac; then Branko, son of Danilo; Ranko Tomic; Dragan Tomic; Dobrivoje Ivkovic; then me; then Mijo Gotovac. That I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not remember Milovan Kuljanin, Mici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the hangar. You were inside the hangar most of the time, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a pan situated in the hangar in the evenings for your toilet habits; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
