utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the day you were taken out in groups to use the toilet outside hangar 6, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the day that can that you used at night was taken out and washed out, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes it was washed; sometimes it wasn't. Somebody was on duty, Dragoslav Kujundzic, called Gago, and the guard would call him out in the morning. He would go out and I do not know what he would do. Then Gago would come back and he would order individuals to take out the bucket and to bring it back in. Sometimes during the day people urinated there, because we were taken out only once during the day, around 3 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you also: in hangar number 6 there are windows around the very top of the hangar, are there not, and they are about 3 metres off the ground, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was some glass up there, but I cannot remember exactly. I just know there was an iron roof structure. It was very hot in those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were standing outside of hangar 6, facing it, the only door that was used into hangar 6 was a small door to the lower right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know there was a door in the corner somehow, towards the -- from the outside it was to the right. They were steel. How big they were I do not know. Behind that door was the bucket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were large hangar doors that were never opened while you were there, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the side of hangar number 6 that the door was on, considered the front of hangar 6, there were no holes in the walls, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were sitting in the middle, but as far as you can remember, around the edges of the hangar the hangar facility, the concrete around the bottom was sealed, so you could not get air and you could not stick your hand out the bottom of the hangar, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went out to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. What you are saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had set up around the back --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all sealed, closed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Around the back of hangar number 6 to the right they had set up some temporary toilet facilities for you, did they not? (12.00)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember there were such toilets at the beginning. Later on there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They took them away. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. About 15 metres from the hangar the prisoners went to dig out a septic tank. There was a plank across that pit and they would take us out, three or four at a time, to stand on that plank to use the toilet. Some soldiers from the road would fire at us, and I think some people were complaining to Esad Delic, but this did not last long. This went on for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. I asked him if they had taken the toilet facilities away. I would hope he would just answer the question. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please answer the question directly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether they removed the toilet. I do not know. I don't remember. I went out very rarely. I do not know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, in the front of hangar number 6 there was a long hose with water, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go to Branko Gotovac. You have no personal knowledge about what happened to him, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Wednesday I talked about Branko Gotovac. I know what happened. I told you. They said some journalists would be coming to number 6 and they came, some black people. I still do not know who they were. They talked for a while and they picked Branko Gotovac. He was first in line. They asked him something. I do not know what. Branko came back to his place. Then the journalists left. Esad Landzo picked out Branko Gotovac and took him out. What he did to him I do not know. I just remember when he brought him back he fell. He was not conscious. There was Branko Gligorevic, who was a nurse, and somebody used the spoon to pull out his tongue. Then he was taken away to the infirmary. He have suffered a lot and Branko survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you have no personal knowledge as to whether the seizure -- the problem that Branko Gotovac had was a heart attack or an attack of diabetes. You have no personal knowledge about why he was sick, do you? You are only speculating. You have no personal knowledge of what happened to Branko Gotovac, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he came back, he said that his stomach had collapsed from beatings and he was complaining of pain all over his body. He complained about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he complained that he was ill, he was taken to the infirmary and received proper medical attention, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I believe you stated he went to the infirmary and he came back recovered. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked also in your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true. How he recovered I do not know. He knows best. He will tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you stated on Wednesday -- you talked about Mr Landzo hitting you at the door of the hangar, did you not, but it would be a surprise to you to know that there are no other witnesses that remember that incident, if you were hit at the door of hangar number 6. Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know which witnesses you will have. I just know what he did to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to Bosko Samoukovic, the only information you have about what may or may not have happened to Bosko Samoukovic is what you have heard from other people, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was an eye witness to that. I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you are saying is you saw Mr Landzo hit him in the back, but that is all you saw, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that and I -- I can always testify to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Scepo Gotovac, you said that you heard -- they took him outside and that you sat there and you counted 450 blows; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I started counting. I counted to about 160 and then I stopped there and then after that I couldn't count any more. That was the first time. The second time I did not count at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your statement on February 20th you claimed that you counted 450 blows, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you have no idea who, if anyone, was hitting Scepo Gotovac, do you, because that was outside the hangar, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know. I know who hit him. I know who took him out and who beat him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was an eye witness, because I know the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you may know who took him out of the hangar and you may know who brought him back in the hangar, but you do not know who was hitting him, if he was hit, outside the hangar, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know who took him out. One was Adem Cosic was holding a knife to his throat, and Hazim Delic and Esad Landzo and Adem Cosic, they took him out and he was beaten there. I heard the cries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know who beat him outside the hangar, do you? You did not see this. You did not witness it. All you can do is speculate; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see, but who else but them would have beat him? Others will speak of that. They will prove it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, that is called speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took him out to beat him. That is what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is called speculation also. You do not know what their purpose was for taking him out. You could not read their minds, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I only saw when they took him out and when they brought him back. That was the first time. The second time he was brought back in he was dead and in the morning -- he spent the night there and in the morning they took him out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go to the Zeljko Klimenta. You have no personal knowledge about what happened to Zeljko Klimenta, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said on Wednesday at the end of July or in early August there was Kujundzic Dragoslav. His nickname was Drago and the guard called out this Drago and ten minutes later they called out Zeljko Klimenta, called Keljo, to take coffee with them. Zeljko went out and about ten minutes later there was a gunshot, and this Drago came back and he said Zeljko was killed and he was crying, and I do not know who did it, who killed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that the guard that had the bullet discharge, you know that was an accident and the guard was crying, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Milovan Kuljanin stated he knew it was an accident and the guard came in crying, would he be lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have nothing against that. Whatever Milovan says I do not know but this is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Cedo Avramovic, he died of natural causes. He died of a heart attack, did he not, in the middle of the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cedo Avramovic, you have no personal knowledge what happened to him. It happened -- whatever happened to him happened outside the hangar, and it happened at night, and you did not see anything, did you, only what you have heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I know that Cedo disappeared. That is what I know. Then I never heard about him, but he was beaten. Esad Landzo beat him about two days. Cedo cried and I do not know when Cedo left or anything. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He said he does not know what happened to him and then goes in and says what he heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you have no personal knowledge on that. Now, I want to go to your statement about the incident that you have talked about with Esad Landzo. Your statement on Wednesday was that Esad Landzo, Hazim Delic, took you out of the hangar, put a mask over your eyes and beat you. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if someone takes you out and puts a mask over your eyes, the truth is you do not know who beat you, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they took off the mask, then I saw them. I was lying down and I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who else it could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, do you know who Zenga is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know each other. He was a child to me but I found out in number 6 I knew his father very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there another name for Zenga? Who is it you think Zenga is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Esad Landzo was called Zenga. That is how they called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where that name comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know that the Landzos were from the Glavaticevo village. That is where his father lived and his father had other children and he worked with me in a ship rent company in Konjic. We would get together. We would smoke together. He was a quiet man, a fine man. I do not know -- I said I didn't know him before I was in number 6 in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified on Wednesday that after the mask was taken off you went back to the hangar and that Esad Landzo beat you again in the door of the hangar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to know that no other witnesses testified to your being beaten in front of them by Esad Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that. I just know what happened to me and I know who beat me, who took me out and who brought me back, and beat me at the door and then I dropped to the floor and I was in a coma and I do not know -- did not know about myself or anything. Then later, when I could walk again, two days later when Esad Landzo took me out to the same place, I lay down on the concrete and he made me pull up the cuff. Then in the right hand he held a little bottle, small bottle. He said: "Do you know what this is?" I said: "I do not know." I said: "Young man, I am not guilty of anything." Then he poured it on my right leg and I do not know if he was going to light it with a lighter or with a match, and then he lit it and then I started jerking it and it was a short time. Then he had something there that he poured over me and then he said to "get up". I got up and then he hit me about twice. He opened the door. There was a plank. He removed it. I walked in. Then later I had a bad burn and I had yellow blisters. It was hurting a lot. All that is true. Later I could not walk and Hazim Delic knows about that and Dragan Povic also knows about that. He was helping me walk out and then I came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you finished, Mr Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am finished. If there is anything else about number 6, tell me, or I would like to finish here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, the story that you just told this tribunal is not what you said on February 20th 1996, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please allow me, it has been five years. In another five years I will forget everything except for the consequences of my wounds. One forgets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to bring to your attention that on February 20th you said that Esad Landzo took you off and ordered you to take off your pants and that he ripped your pants off with a knife and you were standing there naked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not on 20th February. It wasn't on 20th February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. Your Honours. Could he ask him to let me finish the question? It is very difficult for the interpreters I know when we are overlapping like that? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. He was merely correcting your dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gentlemen, please, it wasn't 20th February. It was 20th -- around 20th July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I am sorry. I am referring to your statement that you made on February 20th 1996. In that statement you stated that Mr Landzo ripped your pants off with a knife and you were standing there naked. Did you or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a knife, yes, yes, yes. Yes, it's true. I cannot recall everything, but it's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not what you said in the court Wednesday or today, is it? You said that Mr Landzo told you to pull your pants' legs up, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gentlemen, I have forgotten these things. I do not know how much I am forgetting here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, there is a great difference between ripping your pants off with a knife and standing there naked and, as you said on Wednesday: "He asked me to lift my trouser legs." That is quite a discrepancy, is it not, Mr Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but I did not say nowhere, not in the statement of 26th February, that Esad Landzo ever took my pants off. That is not what I said. I only said about the leg. It is a leg, the pant leg, and my leg. Sejo was not taking off my pants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The court will have this in your possession after your testimony so if you said: "I was standing there naked", then you were lying, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. I object to calling the witness a liar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours and Mr Babic, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not what I said. That is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You would not be telling the truth on February 20th if you said you were standing there naked, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was speaking on Wednesday, that is how I had spoken on the 26th February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that you never said that you were standing there naked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where? Where? I was not able to understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you also -- do you want me to repeat the question, Mr Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that you never said on February 20th 1996 that you were standing there naked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then you also say that he poured petrol on your leg and set it on fire and you were burning for 20 seconds. That is what you said on February 20th, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it was around 20, whether it was around 20, maybe 10, I do not know. It was a short time. I couldn't determine the exact time, whether it was shorter. I do not know. But I saw my leg burning and it hurt. I do not know how long it went on, but I think it went on for a short time --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you also said on Wednesday --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- proof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said on Wednesday. "I saw the flame. I almost lost consciousness. This did not last very long." Did you not say this on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The time, I could have said 20 seconds, maybe 10 seconds, maybe five seconds. I do not know. I was giving the statement to the investigating judge and he said: "How long?" I said: "I do not know." I didn't know how long it was. I was ready to ask him to be -- to kill me so we would stop suffering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for clarification I would like the court to be aware now the secondhand is on the 6, and what a long period of time -- now it is 10 seconds and now it is 20 seconds. On February 20th, you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Excuse me. How could a person who is burning count the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I do not have to answer the questions, your Honour. Mr Babic is the one who allowed 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is what he thought. If I had been there, I would have thought it was a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, probably. I am just trying to bring out the discrepancies in your testimony. Also you said that he extinguished it with a coat on February 20th 1996 and on Wednesday you said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- he covered up the leg and he put it out very quickly. Is that not what you said Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I do not know how it happened. I do not know what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you say you went back to the camp crawling on February 20th 1996, did you not, but you never mentioned crawling back to the camp on Wednesday, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your exact words were: "I went in and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say on Wednesday: "I went in and sat down"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, ladies and gentlemen, on 26th February I gave a statement. It is true that I barely could walk, that I would drop down and then I would get up again, but I cannot remember all of this, and I keep forgetting things. Yes, he kicked me twice when he was taking -- when he was setting me on fire, and there was that plank next to the door to the right, and he opened that door. I walked in and he did not touch me then and I just went straight to my place. That is what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the truth but I cannot recall everything, ladies and gentlemen, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your account of what happened on February 20th 1996 was a lot more dramatic and exaggerated than your account under oath here in this court room, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, please, if I only had another five years, maybe I would not be remembering any of this. I am losing all this from my sight, because I do not want to talk about it any more. I just want -- having come here because I was invited to come here, but other than that. Thank you very much. Thank you very much to the judges for inviting me here to the Hague, to the tribunal to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honours, instead of continuing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, ladies and gentlemen, in five years one forgets, and it is also the age. I do not have the memory. Had I been asked right away, when it was still fresh, but five years had gone by. You can ask me now all you want, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honours, instead of objecting again, I would like the defence counsel to avoid asking the witness to characterise the previous statement, because this is not part of his testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond? He made the statement. It is signed. It will be before the court as evidence in a few moments. The statement that he made on February 20th 1996 is exaggerated and dramatic and not at all related to the statement that he made in this court room on Wednesday. It shows maybe a motive for fabrication, which is also necessary to the impeachment of this witness. I only ask that he answer my one question, because he knows whether his statement of February 20th was exaggerated and more dramatic than his statement that he made on Wednesday. That is the only person that has personal knowledge of that. May I ask the question? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If my memory is correct, much of the things he has been telling you should be the answer to that question. It has been a cumulative experience and one forgets and is likely to forget and he might have been forgetting quite a number of events.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was just asking in summary basically. I will move on, if I may proceed. Mr Babic, on July 15th, when you alleged that Mr Landzo poured petrol on your leg, nobody else witnessed this incident except you, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. It was somewhere around 20th July, but I said it was somewhere around 20th July, not around 15th July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, excluding the date, nobody else witnessed this incident except you, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a guard there. I do not know who it was. He was a bit further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to ask Mr Babic to show his wound to the court again so that the video department might take a photograph, because we would like to introduce the photograph of Mr Babic's injury into evidence as defence exhibit. We, of course, have not been allowed any opportunity to view his wound except briefly on Wednesday. Could we ask Mr Babic to expose that so that the video department can get it on the video camera and also on a still camera so we can preserve it for evidence? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. Let him expose his wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am going to ask the Video Department and Mark to assist me with this, if possible. Mr Babic, would you stand up, please, and wherever the Video Department tells me is the best place for viewing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Can I take off the headphones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I approach too, your Honour? Since I am not technically sure about what happens here, I do not know if we get a still photograph of this so I can -- okay. Thank you. May I approach the witness to look, your Honour, also? Thank you. Photographs are dangerous, are they not? That is how you will take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr Ostberg, was he medically examined at any stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: As far as this wound, I do not know. I do not really know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Did you get a photograph of that? Okay. Thank you, Mr Babic. I just wanted to preserve this for the court's review when they take the evidence back. Thank you very much. In responding to Mr Ostberg, we had asked the prosecution a long time ago to provide any medical documentation that they had and they told us they had no further. So we assume, based upon the representation by the prosecution, that there are no medical records relating to this injury, and therefore I would like to re-urge to the court to grant us permission to have our doctor just briefly look at the wound and tell us what kind of wound it is. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us hear the response to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The position of the prosecution is that if the Trial Chamber deems useful and necessary to have medical expertise done on the leg of Mr Babic, that would certainly be done, and the prosecution has no objection against that, but we assume that an expert should be appointed by the Trial Chamber or by the Registry and not simply pick up any physician here today to do that, whom we do not know anything about. This is the position of the prosecution. We do not object to a medical expertise, but it has to be an expertise done either by the Trial Chamber or the Registry, with the possibility of experts from both parties in the case. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I respond? We have certainly no opposition to the tribunal appointing whatever expert they deem appropriate to examine Mr Babic's leg. We have no problem with that, and just as long as -- at this point, because there is no authentication whatsoever of the injury -- it could have happened 20 years ago, it could have happened last year. It could not be a burn injury whatsoever; it could be a bruise. We just need to know for our own benefit and for the tribunal's benefit what this injury is. Since we have no medical records and Mr Babic never saw a doctor in relation to this, then we have no information about it. Just to authenticate it is what he claims it is, we ask the tribunal to appoint whatever expert they choose. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. (Pause). I think -- we have conferred. Since there is a dispute as to the nature of the injury, the fairest thing is to empanel an independent expert to go into it and determine whether, in fact, this is what it is claimed to be. So it might not be correct to use your own expert, which has not been agreed to by the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. I agree and we will certainly oblige anything that the tribunal thinks is fair in this area. So thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think the fairest thing is to get the Registrar to appoint an independent to examine the witness and determine the nature of the injury, and for how long he has had it. I think that is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we all get home before Christmas, I really only have a couple more questions right now. I would like the court -- we just did receive the interpretation of those documents from the Bosnian government, so I have just two more questions for Mr Babic, and then I will let Mr Moran proceed, but I would like to be able to come back after I have studied these documents just to ask him limited questions referring to those documents only. I only have a few more questions. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Put them to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I proceed? Mr Babic, just for the record I want to make it clear there are no medical records anywhere reflecting the injury on your right ankle, are there? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I am surprised you still continue on that line when we have decided we are getting an independent --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then I will go on to the next question. I just wanted on to the record that there were no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Allow me to say something, if I may. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. Let us hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gentlemen, may I be allowed? When I left the camp it was still wartime. I had no-one to consult. Who could I talk to? There were no doctors. There was no-one. I was at the Military Academy Hospital. I went for treatment. Then I went to Sarajevo. I was living in Alija. There were no doctors, there was nothing. Who would give me a medical examination? So it went on. Five years have gone by. I am honoured to say to the honourable judge, who called me to speak before this court to tell the truth, and I am honoured, but who would look at me? There were no doctors. There were no medicines. I was not even thinking about my own life. That is why I have no medical documentation. That is the reason. Here I am now before this tribunal in the Hague. I feel honoured to have this opportunity to inform you of the truth and tell you how I was burned. It is up to you to judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, would it surprise you to know that the other witnesses with injuries had seen the doctor to the Belgrade Commission in Serbia and they all have medical records reflecting their injuries in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection. This is not something the witness can know and it is arguable whether all the other ones had or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will proceed, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Some other question, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr Babic, on Wednesday you testified on page 287 of the transcript that people kept disappearing from Celebici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know whether they were traded, released? You have no idea what happened to those people that simply disappeared, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Only when I left the camp I learned that they were no longer among the living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I object. He is referring to hearsay, something he learned after he left the camp from other Serbian people in his village. He has no personal knowledge. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Well, you have told me how the Common Law procedure about cross-examination is and I told you from the beginning you take the consequences of your examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then, Mr Babic, would you just answer my question? I asked you if you personally knew what happened to the people that you claim disappeared. You do not, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: Mr Babic, you said that Esad Landzo never came around any more about a week before September 1st, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the truth is that you do not know exactly when he left or where he went, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I just remember that five or six days before I left to Musala, Konjic, he disappeared and I do not know anything more about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to pass the witness now subject to the permission of the tribunal to question him after lunch on the documents that we just received. It would be very brief. May I have permission? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are concluding cross-examination for the time being?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: For the time being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I go out and have a smoke, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: If I smoked, I would go out and have a smoke too. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Did I hear Mr Babic wanting to smoke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to ask your permission if I could to go out and have a cigarette, please. I beg you to allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If it means he remains relaxed, we might let him have a smoke. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We will rise for a few minutes and let him have a smoke. (12.45pm) (Luncheon Adjournment) 21 22 23 24 25 (2.15pm) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please call the witness. The witness is still on his oath and still under cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: May it please the court --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Excuse me just for one second. I was just going to offer the documents I promised the tribunal earlier. This is the statement of Mirko Babic from February 20th, 1996 and the photographs taken here in the court room to be marked as defence exhibits for the court's review please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: No objection. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I have no objection to his extra judicial statement being taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Mark the documents "Defence exhibits 1 and 2".

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement will be marked document D1/4 and the photograph D1/-- D2/4. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Cross-examination by MR MORAN

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Mr Babic, my name is Tom Moran, one of the defence lawyers here. I am going to be asking you some questions. If I speak too fast and/or you do not understand the question, will you stop me and ask me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, I would like to thank you for the smoke break. I am also a smoker and needed that break also. I would like to discuss a few things with you this afternoon. First, there was a lot of talk about your statement, the statement that you gave to the office of the prosecutor back in February 1996. I would like to talk with you a little bit about how that statement was given. Did you go to an office or did they come to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to an office and gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were two people there, Mr D'Hooge from the office of the prosecutor and an interpreter; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not read or writing English, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, Mr D'Hooge would ask you some questions and they would be interpreted for you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometimes he would ask you things you did not remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said a little earlier today that sometimes when you did not know, he would keep asking you and tell you to guess; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was not saying that, nothing like that. He asked me what did I know, whether I remembered this and what I knew I said, but there was no persuasion or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for instance, you said earlier, when you were talking to Ms McMurrey, that when you were asked about how many people were in building number 22, you said you did not know and he kept saying: "Make an approximation"; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He kept telling you he wanted the statement shorter and he wanted you to hurry it up. You said that, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards the end, and I was avoiding it too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you avoiding, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just so that we wouldn't go so long, I was just saying what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, you probably remembered things better back in February of 1996 than you do today, do not you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it has been a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A long time. I am forgetting quite a bit. I said before in another five years I would have forgotten almost everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I believe you testified last Wednesday, and stop me if I am wrong, that in 1967, when you became a forest guard, you went to MUP and MUP gave you a permit to carry the pistol and the pistol itself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was because you needed the pistol because of your job as a forest guard; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in April 1992 you were not a forest guard any more, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four or five months before the war itself, I retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in April 1992 you did not need a pistol to be a forest guard any more, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody took that weapon away from me. I had the right to carry it. Nobody wanted it. I kept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but in April of 1992 you did not need that pistol to be a forest guard any more, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a forest guard, no, but it was my weapon. I had bought it and I had legal permit from the Konjic municipality and I kept with it me. Nobody asked me to give it in, so I kept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you testified a few minutes ago that MUP gave you the weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you buy it from them or did they issue it to you, lend it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I bought it for my own money in a shop in Sarajevo and told the MUP in Konjic and they issued me a permit to carry it and that was in 1967. That pistol stayed with me at my place until 22nd May 1992, when Midhat took it from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So MUP did not give you the pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, MUP, MUP was the one that issued it to me in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you said you just bought the pistol -- you just said you bought the pistol in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So MUP did not give you the pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not MUP, no, no, no. I just reported it to MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To get a permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in order to get the permit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was so --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no problem about that. They gave -- I sent in a request and within three days I got the permit, and there was no problem after that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was because you needed it for your job; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for my job, because I was in the field. I was an official person and I was a forest guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to jump forward a little bit and talk about building number 22. Do you remember what the inside of building 22 looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were white walls. As far as I can recall, and that is about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any windows you could look out of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall. It seems to me that maybe up there but no, I was not even looking. I do not know what there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if there were windows that you could look out of, you do not remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember any of it. I was not even looking so I do not know if there was anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement of February 20th -- in fact, in your testimony here also last week -- when certain incidents happened, you were pretty specific about the time. You said one thing happened at 9 o'clock in the morning. Something else happened at 10 o'clock in the morning. Did you have a watch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone take away your watch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I remember something from number 22. In the evenings some people came. I do not know who it was. They came to the door and said whoever has any watches or gold, they should turn it in to them, and if they did not get it, they will come and control. Then I remember that some did get up and turn it over to them, but -- and that is how I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not have a watch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how could you tell that something happened at 9 o'clock in the morning or 10 o'clock in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were just guessing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was guessing. I didn't have a watch. It was around that time. I was not even thinking how long something went on, whether it went on for minutes or for hours. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, for instance, when you testified last Wednesday that another day someone came in about 9 o'clock, the time was just a guess?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you mean? Can you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On page 275, line 25, and continuing on to the next page of the transcript from last Wednesday, you said: "Another day about 9 o'clock he came again and he kicked me with his boot." You were just guessing about the time, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not true that I said 9. I do not remember the dates, at what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it is in the transcript, that is a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that I said that, 9 o'clock. I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So if it is in the transcript, that would be a mistake; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know that I said 9 o'clock. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to also talk to you a little bit about Slobodan Babic. He was your cousin; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He went to Radava, did he not? He was there with you, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had been beaten up, like you had been, before he got to Radava; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was all bloody in his face and his arms and his head, just like I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was before either of you got to Celebici; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was before, but I do not remember Slobodan arriving to Celebici with me that night. I do not recall. I was in bad shape. I know that there was a truck with a canopy. I only know that I arrived in front of number 22 and I was put inside. I do not recall Slobodan, but I remember that I saw him two days later lying next to me, and I saw how he was. He couldn't hear and he couldn't see and the other witnesses will tell that something in his mouth was injured, and I remember well that a bottle filled with water came from somewhere -- I do not know if the guards brought it -- and I remember that they were trying to give it to him drop by drop, but it couldn't get through, but he was dying and I was watching as he was dying, and I can also say that his son came, Predrag, and he was there two or three days, and he was watching his own father dying, but he couldn't look at him, and his son was released soon, and he stayed in 22. His son was about 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and again my question was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see how much I do not recall, you know, so much time has passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me try my question again and see if you can answer it this time. Slobodan Babic had been beaten severely at Radava, before he got there; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, badly beaten, just like I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was before either one of you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us over our heads, chest, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was before either one of you had been to the Celebici camp; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it was before. I just know that I arrived in Celebici to number 22 and I didn't see Slobodan, but I saw him badly beaten two days later in number 22. He was very badly beaten at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and when you were at Radava with him, and he was beaten there, that beating and those injuries occurred before either one of you got to Celebici; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember anything. I just know that in Radava I lost him there. When I climbed on to the truck I do not recall anything until two days later I saw him in number 22, where he was beaten up. I do not recall anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Let us try this a little bit differently. Once you left Radava and went to Celebici, you never went back to Radava, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you and Slobodan Babic were injured while you were at Radava that was before either one of you got to Celebici; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were beaten up on the way from the village of Bijelovcina, where we had stopped, where two women bought out Slobodan and he was already bloodied. He was bloodied like I was. When we arrived in Konjic, in the sports hall in Konjic municipality, then they did not touch us. We were there, both of us, but the next day, the evening of the 23rd they called us out, and we went in the truck from Radava. The truck stopped and we entered into this hotel and there were three of four of them there. One had his foot bandaged and he started beating us. I said there was this Ismeta girl, and she did not allow that. I do not know if she worked there or not. She said: "You are not going to touch the forest guard." She brought some eggs and I'll never forget that she gave us water to drink and I'm very thankful to her. She saved us just by giving us water there. Half an hour later we started off again. I said that on Wednesday. Then after that I didn't see Slobodan. I went on to the truck and then I arrived in number 22 in Celebici and they put me in there, and at that moment I do not recall if Slobodan came with me at that time. I only remember that two days later I saw him in number 22 beaten up. He was dying. He was dying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And do not ask me anything else about Slobodan because I do not know who beat him, what they did to him and where. That is all I know. I heard from some statements that he was somewhere in a motel, that he was being beaten there. Some others say it was in a school, but Dr Petko can give you that evidence. He knows the most about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, let me make a deal with you; okay? I will ask a question and I will try to make the question as narrow as possible. If you do not understand it, I will repeat it or rephrase it; okay? In return, will you just answer the question that I ask? Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically what you are telling the tribunal -- basically what your testimony about Slobodan Babic is is you and he were both injured when you arrived at Radava; that is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were split up at Radava?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they -- you were taken to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And two days later Slobodan Babic was brought to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time he was brought there he was terribly injured, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had been tortured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he couldn't hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And somebody, before he got to Celebici, had been putting guns in his mouth; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe. I cannot say that exactly. Probably something was put in his mouth and that is how the injury resulted so he couldn't swallow anything. He was very ill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in that condition when he got to Celebici; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified back on Wednesday that Hazim Delic, my client, was the commandant of the camp, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that he was a deputy to someone else, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me. I could not distinguish the two. I said we called him Mr Commander, but who he was -- that is what I said on Wednesday -- I said I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not really know who the commander of the camp at Celebici was, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who was the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would not want anybody to get the impression and to think that you were saying that someone was commander, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said so. I repeat again we called Hazim Delic "Mr Commander". Whether he was a commander, whether he was a deputy, what rank he was, I really do not know. I do not know anything about that. I do not know who was the commander in the prison, but I only know that is how we called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, Mr Delic, what kind of uniform did he wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything different about his uniform from everybody else's uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot describe it to you. I mostly looked in front of me. I didn't look left and right. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was -- when he walked, how did he walk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally. He was hurt somewhere. I do not know. He was limping a little bit. He carried an automatic rifle and that is how he walked. He was a hardworking young man and we all feared him terribly, when he would come in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he carrying a crutch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not in late May, early June of 1992 whether he was wearing a cast on one leg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have just a second, just a couple of seconds to confer with co-counsel? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Babic, when you were a forest guard -- I do not know how it is in the former Yugoslavia, but in America, where I come from, working in the forest is a very dangerous profession. People get hurt all the time. Is it that way in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know. I just know what I did and I didn't have any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Mrs Residovic, the witness is for you now. Cross-examination by MS RESIDOVIC MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, Mr President. Mr Babic, my name is Edina Residovic. I am defence counsel of Zejnil Delalic. May I start the cross-examination? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr Babic, you said in your earlier testimony that after the cessation from the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina you organised watch duty round your houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not organise. We just kept -- I was on duty in front of my house. Occasionally we'd go out in the evenings and in the mornings but there was absolutely no organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question by Mr Turone, you said this was at the beginning of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of February 22nd in 1996 you said that this happened after the Assembly at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr President, may I be allowed to show a short videotape to the witness to remind him a little? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: What is the thing you want to remind him of? Put that to him. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The Assembly that the witness is referring to now and in his previous statement and in the testimony before this court, as he is talking about two different dates, 1991 and April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't say anything about 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is what is recorded in your statement of February 20th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what's written there but this was in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr President, some of those questions are a component part of the introduction of the indictment from which some of the charges against my defendant emerge. That is why this is important for me, and the videotape lasts less than half a minute? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If you choose to do that, it is okay. You can get the videotape. I really do not see the importance of it. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I would like to ask the technicians to give you insert number 1 and, your Honours, I would like to supply you with a translation of the text of the speaker on that videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it an agreed translation? Has the prosecution had an opportunity to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is quite new for us. Could we have a translation too? MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, of course. Maybe we could put it on the ELMO, if you like. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): For the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me, we believe that this is not relevant to the case and it is something about which the witness already said he does not know anything about. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, what is relevant for the defence I think should be allowed the defence. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Frankly, I did not see this trail of events relating to any date. If you are interested in a date, you can introduce the dates and during consideration I think one can take cognisance of the differences in the two dates. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, reference is made to the Assembly and not the date. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The Assembly sitting will not authenticate any dates. It will not be there and nobody will know whatever whether it sat on that date or any other date. I do not see the relevance of it. If you have other things to say in order to contradict the witness, go ahead and do that, because it has no relevance whatsoever. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): We would like to remind the witness, because it is a relevant Assembly meeting, not just any Assembly meeting. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I am not sure he is a member of the Assembly, is he? The witness is not a member of that assembly. He did not take part in any of the things there. If that is your case, put it to him, but I do not need any of this videotape. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honour, his behaviour and the behaviour of others was affected substantively by that Assembly, so that is why I would request that we show this video. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If you are saying it is historical fact, state that and we can carry on with the evidence. You can say that. There is no point putting on a video. The video is completely irrelevant to what you want to say. The historical fact has happened. The Assembly held certain things. Then you can go ahead, if also he is familiar with that. If he is not familiar with that, that is a different matter. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): In your statement, you said that after that you were very scared and at that Assembly the external nation was threatened of the Muslim people. Is that what you were afraid of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. I and my neighbourhood, we were afraid that something could happen. We did not know who would attack us. We were living together, all of us together, until the last day. We did not talk about Muslims or Serbs or Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you piece answer my direct question? At the mentioned Assembly Radovan Karadzic threatened with the external nation of the Muslim people. Were you afraid of that threat to the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do not ask me these things. I do not know anything about that, what Karadzic said, who said. I do not know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you do not know, even though you do not know, did you set up guards to watch your houses; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There weren't guards. We were just -- we looked after our houses and stables. We had shifts. I have experience. Why was I afraid? Why did I keep duty. If His Honour allows me, I will tell him why I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please answer my question. On February 20th, talking to the investigator of the prosecution, you said that you put guards round your houses. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were not guards. We just watched over our houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that certainly is different from what you are now saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you imply by "guards". We were simply watching over our houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, you live in the municipality of Konjic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know on May 4th Konjic was shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know. Maybe it was but I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that after that day Konjic was heavily shelled on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. Maybe. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a citizen of the municipality of Konjic; yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go back to some of the questions affecting you personally, Mr Babic you are a forest guard until 1973 in Pren, Konjic. From 1973 you are an unskilled worker in Neretva of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, until 31st August 1991, you were a forest guard of private woods in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1984 I again became a forest guard, a private forest guard in the municipality of Konjic, but my manager was the same over state run forests and private forest, Dzemo Karabegovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in 1973 after disciplinary proceedings against you you were transferred to the position of an unskilled worker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no disciplinary proceedings. They simply told me: "You are changing your job."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that demotion in relation to your previous post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. At that time there were redundancies. There were 24 foresters and that is why I had to change my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1973 there were no redundancies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in 1986. Yes, there were in the forest maintenance enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you did not abuse your official position and as a result were transferred to the position of an unskilled worker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I am saying. I didn't commit any offence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were pensioned off on 31st August 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to Mr Turone's question you said that in May 1992 you were a forester?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I retired four, five months before that. That is all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, you were not a forester in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I object to this question. The witness has already answered more than one time to this request of clarification. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Allow me, Mr President, because some of the answers were not precise, since I have the exact information, I wish to clear these points up in the interests of the defence of my client. At the same time we wish to establish whether this witness is speaking the truth in reference to those facts. May I continue? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. You are free. You can continue. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Pensioners in our country cannot have weapons as an official instrument of work. Did you return your pistol, because you no longer had any official duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody asked for my pistol back. I can tell you also that just before retirement, two months before that, I asked because I was hunting a little, I asked to have a hunting rifle, if they would give me a permit for a hunting rifle and I got that permit, but I didn't buy a rifle. I had the right to hunt and the pistol I had was my own property. Nobody wanted it, and I could have carried it until my death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not return it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no need. It is my own personal pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Babic, you said that you were a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dusko Bendjo and Risto Vukalo, your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Miro Duricic was President of the SDS in your local community and you were the secretary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If these other persons were to confirm these allegations do they know --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. The defence may not impeach this witness with what other persons may or may not have said or may come to say in future. It is the submission of the prosecution that the defence may bring in other witnesses to say certain things. If the defence wishes, they may also attempt to bring in documents which contain information different than that said by the witness, but this witness has no way of knowing what other witnesses have or have not said or are going to say. The witness thus may not be asked about what other persons have said. Asking him this is improper. Asking him about what other people said, asking his opinion on what other people may have said or may come to say in the future, asking his knowledge about other people having said whatever is improper, unfair to the witness and potentially misleading. If the defence wants to introduce some statements, the defence can do that, but the defence cannot introduce other documents through this witness if they concern something which other people said. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually all counsel has suggested is whether he could accept the truth if others came to say that. He is free to reject it. There is nothing stopping him rejecting it. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr President, my colleague, Ms McMurrey, informed you this morning that we have just received a large number, 130, statements of various witnesses made in 1992. Since we were not able to receive the full translation and we will be using the transcripts as evidence in the proceedings -- my colleagues informing me that we do have the translations now. May we, your Honour, give you the translations of the statements that we announced this morning, which may serve as a basis for addressing questions to the witness. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I do not know how regular that is. If you have any questioning against the witness in cross-examination, you can put it to him basing it on whatever information you have about him. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Very well. In that case I will try and not mention the names of witnesses, as the prosecutor has suggested, but I would like to ask a question of Mr Babic. Mr Babic, do you know Cecez Lazar from Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is about 15 kms away from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in touch with him during 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. That is not true. That is more than a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your duty was to cooperate with Zivak Strahinja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given a rifle M48?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. If other people say something else, does that mean they are not telling the truth. I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. The witness cannot be asked -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He has already answered it. I do not see what you are objecting to. He said "no" and I think that is conclusive. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr Babic, did you have injuries and burns before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Jaric Marijan, a forester, born in Ibar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a good friend of his?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He lived in Celebici near the restaurant called "Jezero"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were friends together and from time to time you would have a drink?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever burn plaster with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three or four years before the war did you catch fire together with Marijan in dealing with this plaster?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If medical documentation and that man were to say the opposite, you are saying that they are not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. I do not remember that, nor did that happen, nor did I ever set fire to anything with Marijan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with which municipality the village of Bijelovcina would belong to if Konjic had been occupied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. It was all the same to me. The only thing was for me to be free. That is all I cared about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you never consulted with anyone over political questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because I was never interested in politics. I had my job to do. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that after interrogation a large number of people were released from Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Some people were released. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that this was done by the information commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat a question once again. You were not exposed to any burns several years before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: This is the last of the cross-examinations, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I believe subject to re-cross, if the prosecution directs. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are suggesting some other questions you had?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I have just received one of the documents in English -- we have not received one of them, have we? Okay. We just received it from -- the translation not even a few seconds ago. If I might have just one moment to read it please. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Because it is better you conclude whatever questions you want to ask before re-examination. That is a tidier way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have just one question to ask from the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: how many persons from his village were taken to
utterances.text: To Celebici camp to number 6 and the sports hall Musala in Konjic 45 people were taken. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Mrs McMurrey, can you continue with your questions now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, just briefly. Further cross-examination by MS MCMURREY:

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Babic, do you know a Risto Vukalo?

utterances.speaker: how many persons from his village were taken to
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a neighbour of yours, was he not?

utterances.speaker: how many persons from his village were taken to
utterances.text: Yes, a neighbour, a little bit further away, 1 km.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Risto Vukalo made a statement saying that you were responsible for cooperating with Strahinja Zivak in distributing the arms in your village, he would be lying?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
